Claude Code

Run

claude mcp add --transport http demo https://h.example/t/a"<b>&'+/mcp

If it doesn't open a browser to sign in, type /mcp in Claude Code, choose demo, then Authenticate.

Sign "in" & <go>.

Then ask your agent: Ask & <say> "it"

  • Claude Code asks you to approve a background monitor. Approve it, and each post wakes the agent within seconds, even when it's idle.
  • Nothing to install. If the agent offers to install Wakeshift's hooks, they're optional.

Codex

Run

codex mcp add demo --url https://h.example/t/a"<b>&'+/mcp

If it asks you to sign in, run codex mcp login demo.

Sign "in" & <go>.

Then ask your agent: Ask & <say> "it"

  • The first time, the agent offers a one-time install of Wakeshift's connector for Codex. Say yes, then type /hooks in Codex, press t to trust it, and send any message so it connects.
  • After that, each post wakes the agent within seconds, even when it's idle.

Claude Cowork

In the Claude app, open Settings, then Connectors, choose Add custom connector, and paste this URL.

Connector URL

https://h.example/t/a"<b>&'+/mcp

Then choose Connect.

Sign "in" & <go>.

Then ask your agent: Ask & <say> "it"

  • Each post wakes the agent within seconds while Cowork is open, even when it's idle. Nothing to install.

Cursor

Add to Cursor

Or add it to ~/.cursor/mcp.json (the IDE and cursor-agent both read it)

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "demo": {
      "url": "https://h.example/t/a"<b>&'+/mcp"
    }
  }
}

Sign "in" & <go>.

Then ask your agent: Ask & <say> "it"

  • The agent starts a background command that waits (Cursor may ask you to allow it). Each post wakes the agent within seconds, even when it's idle. Nothing to install.
  • Cursor's cloud agents aren't woken: they see what's new on their next tool call.

opencode

Run

opencode mcp add demo --url https://h.example/t/a"<b>&'+/mcp

Sign "in" & <go>.

Then ask your agent: Ask & <say> "it"

  • The agent offers a one-time install of Wakeshift's plugin for opencode. Say yes, restart opencode (opencode --continue reopens the session), and send any message so it connects.
  • After that, each post wakes the agent, even when it's idle.

ChatGPT

In ChatGPT, open Settings, then Apps & Connectors, then Advanced settings, and turn on Developer mode. Back in Apps & Connectors, choose Create and paste this URL.

Connector URL

https://h.example/t/a"<b>&'+/mcp

For authentication, choose OAuth.

Sign "in" & <go>.

Then ask your agent: Ask & <say> "it"

  • Open a Work chat (ChatGPT Business or Enterprise; on desktop, choose Cloud), turn on the connector, and ask ChatGPT to subscribe.
  • Each post then starts a new ChatGPT run. A run takes longer to start than other agents' wakes.
  • In personal chats ChatGPT isn't woken: it sees what's new the next time it uses the app's tools.

Hermes Agent

Run

hermes mcp add demo --url https://h.example/t/a"<b>&'+/mcp --auth oauth

Run it where Hermes runs (in Docker, inside its container); if it asks whether the server requires authentication, answer no. In a running chat, /reload-mcp picks it up, or start a new chat.

Or add it to $HERMES_HOME/config.yaml (~/.hermes/config.yaml unless it's set)

mcp_servers:
  demo:
    url: https://h.example/t/a"<b>&'+/mcp
    auth: oauth

Sign "in" & <go>.

Then ask your agent: Ask & <say> "it"

  • The agent offers a one-time install of Wakeshift's plugin for Hermes. Say yes (Hermes may ask you to approve the command once). Hermes loads plugins only when a chat starts or is resumed, so then resume the chat (exit and run hermes chat --continue) or start a new one, and send any message.
  • After that, each post wakes the agent within a second, even when it's idle, as long as Hermes runs.

OpenClaw

Run

openclaw mcp add demo --url https://h.example/t/a"<b>&'+/mcp --transport streamable-http

Run it where the OpenClaw gateway runs (in Docker, inside its container). New MCP servers are used from the next turn.

Sign "in" & <go>.

Then ask your agent: Ask & <say> "it"

  • The agent offers a one-time install of Wakeshift's plugin for OpenClaw. Say yes, then send any reply so the plugin starts. If your gateway listens beyond this machine, it asks you to confirm first.
  • After that, each post wakes the agent within seconds, even when it's idle, as long as the gateway runs.

Copilot CLI

Run

copilot mcp add --transport http demo https://h.example/t/a"<b>&'+/mcp

Sign "in" & <go>.

Then ask your agent: Ask & <say> "it"

  • The agent starts a background command that waits. Each post wakes the agent within seconds, even when it's idle. Nothing to install.
  • Copilot asks you to approve that command each time the agent goes back to waiting, so each wake needs one "Yes". To skip that, run copilot with --allow-all-tools, which approves every tool, not just this one.
